'''Roger Malina''' (born July 6, 1950) is an American [[physicist]], [[astronomer]], [[Executive Editor]] of [[Leonardo (journal)|''Leonardo Publications'']] by [[Leonardo, the International Society for the Arts, Sciences and Technology|Leonardo, the International Society of Arts, Sciences and Technology]] (published by [[MIT Press]]) and [[distinguished professor]] of arts and technology, and professor of physics at the [[University of Texas at Dallas]].

==Education and career==
Malina obtained his [[Bachelor of Science]] in physics from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1972, and his Ph.D. in astronomy from the University of California, Berkeley, in 1979.<ref name="oamp-cv">[http://www.oamp.fr/people/malina/ Curriculum vitae], Observatoire Astronomique de Marseille-Provence, downloaded 19. November 2011</ref> He was principal investigator for the NASA Extreme Ultraviolet Explorer Satellite at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name="malina-about"/> He is former director of the ''Observatoire Astronomique de Marseille Provence'' (OAMP) and of the Laboratoire d'Astrophysique de Marseille in [[Marseille]], and member of its observational cosmology group, which investigates the nature of [[dark matter]] and [[dark energy]].<ref name="malina-about"/><ref>[http://www.oamp.fr/infoglueDeliverLive/Pages+Speciales/Page_Print?contentId=647 Observatoire Astronomique de Marseille-Provence, Département Gassendi], downloaded 19. November 2011</ref><ref>[http://www.asc-cybernetics.org/2011/?page_id=427 Roger Malina], American Society for Cybernetics, 2011, downloaded 19. November 2011</ref>

Malina is president of the ''Association Leonardo'' in France, which fosters connections between the arts, sciences and technology, and has been the editor-in-chief of [[Leonardo (journal)|''Leonardo magazine'']] at [[MIT Press]] since 1982.<ref name="malina-about"/> He is also member of the Mediterranean Institute for Advanced Study (''Institut Méditerranéen de Recherches Avancées'', IMERA),<ref name="malina-about">[http://malina.diatrope.com/about/ Roger Malina], on his own site, downloaded 19. November 2011</ref> which he has helped to set up<ref name="malina-about"/> and which aims at contributing to interdisciplinarity and which places emphasis on the human dimensions of the sciences.<ref>[http://www.imera.fr/index.php/en/component/content/article/271.html The Aix-Marseille Institute for Advanced Study], IMERA, downloaded 19. November 2011</ref> He is member of the jury for the [[Buckminster Fuller Challenge]] 2011.<ref>[http://challenge.bfi.org/jurors The Buckminster Fuller Challenge: Jury], downloaded 19. November 2011</ref>

Malina serves on the Advisory Council of [[METI (Messaging Extraterrestrial Intelligence)]]. In 2011, Malina was appointed as [[distinguished professor]] of art and technology<ref name="malina-about"/> and professor of physics{{Citation needed|date=January 2012}} at the [[University of Texas at Dallas]], where he commenced teaching in Spring 2012.<ref>[http://coursebook.utdallas.edu/search/rxm116130 Class Profile: Special Topics in Arts and Technology], University of Texas at Dallas, downloaded 19. November 2011</ref> His specialty in astrophysics is space instrumentation. His current work focuses on connections between science and art.

==Personal life==
Malina is the son of [[Frank Malina]], who was a research engineer in rocket propulsion, second director of the [[NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory]], and kinetic artist and founder of ''Leonardo Journal''.

In 1986, Malina married British Internet content pioneer and educator [[Christine Maxwell]]. They have three children, sons Xavier (born 1988) and Yuri (born 1990) and daughter Giselle (born 1991).
